comparison.objective: Post a packet completely through a spring-flap slot into a closed drop box; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber to achieve safe repeatable carriage stopping.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-730 tests packet grasp choice, flap actuation, constrained insertion, release, and follow-up pushing where the hand cannot enter. Candidate tests small hex-key alignment, captive-setscrew manipulation, collar counterholding/rotation, tool reacquisition, bounded tightening, and iterative diagnosis from impacts.
comparison.success_condition: PR-730 succeeds when the packet rests wholly inside and the flap closes within 5 mm. Candidate succeeds only after two compliant physical cycles without bottoming, overload, excessive rebound, hard-stop strike, or post-lock collar drift.
comparison.reason: Both involve contact-rich manipulation, but packet insertion through a passive flap neither adjusts a retained mechanism nor demonstrates setting-dependent energy absorption and retention.
